strings: In Booty Bay, Drizzlik reports that the boots are taking shape, but the skins you supplied will not cover the inner layers. Drizzlik proposes filling them out with cheaper, thicker hides from crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti.

Drizzlik has settled the rough form of the boots and says they are coming along nicely, yet the skins from Supply and Demand do not go far enough for the insides. Nobody will ever see those layers, so Drizzlik will make do with thicker, cheaper hides from the crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti.

Drizzlik's sales pitch promises the finest workmanship and boots of pure, top-grade saltwater crocolisk hide. Drizzlik likens the boots to sausages: they look great, they taste great, and they are said to hold only the finest ingredients. It is safer, and more enjoyable, to trust the maker and not look too closely at what is really inside.

Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind.

Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

Confirming the unnatural presence on the isle confirms the baron's highest hopes: the legendary artifact is real. Yet claiming it will not be simple. The Stone of the Tides carries a potent magical curse that Revilgaz recognizes he cannot break alone, requiring the expertise of an experienced wizard before any recovery can begin.

In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those with library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn has set aside royal funds for the work, opening these accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars.

While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor guide Stormwind’s defenses and court in King Varian’s absence, young King Anduin turns royal support toward learning. He funds copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals, so the kingdom’s past can be preserved and studied. Within Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library keeps these written accounts and copies them for those in royal service.

Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Librarian Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from the ancient histories of the Eastern Kingdoms to accounts of distant lands, offering knowledge of conflicts beyond the capital.

This final mission from Commander Althea Ebonlocke directs Alliance adventurers into the crypts of eastern Raven Hill Cemetery. With the Night Watch spread thin defending Darkshire, outsiders must enter the tombs to exterminate the teeming plague spreaders. It marks the culmination of the town guard's direct military campaign to contain the undead overrun.

Darkshire stands almost entirely isolated, abandoned by the Stormwind military and reliant entirely on its own civilian militia, the Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has exhausted her limited manpower simply guarding the crossroads, town perimeter, and supply lines. As the restless dead multiply throughout Duskwood, the commander has no choice but to deputize wandering champions to carry the fight directly into the shadowed recesses of Raven Hill.

The eastern mausoleum in Raven Hill Cemetery represents one of the most hazardous concentrations of undeath in the region. Unlike the open barrows, this stone crypt teems with plague spreaders—ghouls bearing corrupting afflictions capable of sickening the living. Clearing out twenty of these abominations buys precious breathing room for the weary Night Watch, ensuring Darkshire does not face a coordinated undead surge from the west.

The Night Watch is stretched thin across all of Duskwood. With Stormwind providing no official troops, Commander Althea Ebonlocke barely has enough guards to hold Darkshire's perimeter and monitor the roads, leaving no spare militia to clear deep, fortified crypts like Raven Hill.

In the pirate haven of Booty Bay, Whiskey Slim finds himself in dire trouble with his captain. During a violent storm off the coast of the Hinterlands, Slim tapped into a seized crate of Pupellyverbos Port, only to lose the bottles to the churning sea. To escape a brutal flogging, he needs an adventurer to retrieve his misplaced grog.

Whiskey Slim's crew was battling severe weather off the Overlook Cliffs, with the shore of the Hinterlands looming nearby, when the sailor sought a dose of liquid courage. His ship had seized a crate of Pupellyverbos Port from a privateer vessel sailing toward Stormwind. Facing waves that threatened to swallow their ship whole, Slim broke into the captain's crate, but a sudden surge swept the bottles right over the side.

Back in Booty Bay, the clock is ticking down as the ship prepares to weigh anchor. Slim dreads facing the cat-o'-nine-tails once his commanding officer realizes the confiscated port is missing. He seeks someone willing to bring back twelve bottles before his theft comes to light.

Krinkle Goodsteel points you to Fire Plume Ridge, a simmering volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where the lava lake at the top is hot enough to forge the stem of a skeletal key. Afterward you carry it to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands.

Forging the stem of the key takes two bars of thorium and fierce heat. The thorium is yours to find, but Krinkle Goodsteel can help with the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, and it only needs dipping in the lava lake on top of Fire Plume Ridge. The lava does the rest, fusing thorium and bone together.

Krinkle Goodsteel has done their part. To finish the key, you will need to talk to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands again. The key from the lava is still unfinished, and the work so far is preparation for an assault.

Arbington calls the key quite costly, but says it is still unfinished. The foe all this work has been aimed at is in Andorhal: Araj the Summoner, a lich who ranks among the most powerful of the Scourge.

Nimboya has returned from Orgrimmar to the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale to search for Yenniku, the youngest son of his chieftain. Suspecting the Bloodscalp tribe holds the youth captive, the scout asks you to hunt their warriors and take their tusks to demonstrate your strength.

At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nimboya speaks of a grim fate looming over Yenniku, the youngest son of the Darkspear chieftain. In accordance with an old tribal custom, the boy had been placed among the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub. When the Darkspear tribe departed their homeland alongside the orc warchief Thrall, Yenniku was left behind and lost. Sent back from distant Orgrimmar, Nimboya has undertaken the responsibility of finding the chieftain's son and bringing him to safety.

Nimboya believes the Bloodscalp tribe now holds Yenniku. He demands proof that an adventurer is strong enough to hunt them. You are directed north to hunt Bloodscalp trolls and gather nine of their tusks. Bringing these trophies back to Grom'gol Base Camp proves your martial prowess and begins a longer pursuit to locate the chieftain's boy, leading directly into the hunt known as Headhunting.

Yenniku is the youngest son of the Darkspear tribe's chieftain. By tribal custom, he was given to the Gurubashi trolls in Zul'Gurub, but he became separated from his people when the Darkspears left the region.

Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers arriving at the hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Recognizing a fellow battle-tested wanderer, he arranges an introduction to the expedition's leader, the renowned huntsman Hemet Nesingwary.

Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, and he can tell a seasoned combatant when he sees one. Nesingwary reserves his fellowship for proven veterans, and Barnil believes the old marksman might be convinced to share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured the trials of battle.

Nesingwary personally oversees the stalking of raptors, while his comrades Ajeck and Sir Erlgadin tutor hunters in the ways of tigers and panthers.
